column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the thief being found during a break-in and being struck, both in passive forms.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew retains “in his hand,” rather than simply “in his possession.”
The Hebrew joins the best of his field and the best of his vineyard with “and.”
The Hebrew does not separately add “whole” to the field.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew preserves the image of stretching his hand against his neighbor’s property.
The Hebrew literally says “this is it,” rather than expressly “this is mine.”
The Hebrew says the animal was “captured,” rather than using the specific verb for stealing.
The Hebrew says an oath “by the LORD,” rather than “before the LORD.”
